PS 9.1 | Electric Current and Ohm’s Law

Student Solution Key

Solutions

  1. Conceptual Explanation:
  • Electric current ($I$): rate of charge flow through a conductor.
  • Voltage ($V$): electric potential difference or “pressure” driving the current.
  • Resistance ($R$): opposition to current flow in the conductor.
  • Units: $I$ (A = C/s), $V$ (V = J/C), $R$ ($\Omega$ = V/A)
  1. a) Calculate the resistance in the circuit.
    b) Explain why doubling the voltage would double the current.

Parent formula:

$V = IR$ (Ohm’s Law)

$V = 230~\text{V}$
$I = 1.75~\text{A}$

a) $R = \frac{V}{I}$
$R = \frac{230}{1.75}$
$R = 131~\Omega$

$R = 131~\Omega$

  • b) Ohm’s Law: $I = \frac{V}{R}$. If $R$ is constant, doubling $V$ doubles $I$.
  1. a) What is the current flowing through the circuit?
    b) If the resistor is replaced with a $1.00~\text{k}\Omega$ resistor, how does the current change?

Parent formula:
$I = \frac{V}{R}$ (Ohm’s Law)

$V = 9.00~\text{V}$
$R_1 = 470~\Omega$
$R_2 = 1.00~\text{k}\Omega$

a) $I_1 = \frac{9.00}{470}$
$I_1 = 0.0191~\text{A}$
b) $I_2 = \frac{9.00}{1000}$
$I_2 = 0.00900~\text{A}$
Current decreases as resistance increases.

$I_1 = 0.0191~\text{A}$
$I_2 = 0.00900~\text{A}$

  1. What is the resistance of a microwave drawing $12.5~\text{A}$ at $120~\text{V}$?

Parent formula:
$R = \frac{V}{I}$ (Ohm’s Law)

$V = 120~\text{V}$
$I = 12.5~\text{A}$

$R = \frac{V}{I}$
$R = \frac{120}{12.5}$
$R = 9.60~\Omega$

$R = 9.60~\Omega$

  1. a) What voltage must be applied across a $33.0~\Omega$ LED requiring $15.0~\text{mA}$?
    b) Why is the direction of current flow important for LEDs?

Parent formula:
$V = IR$ (Ohm’s Law)

$R = 33.0~\Omega$
$I = 15.0~\text{mA} = 0.0150~\text{A}$

a) $V = IR$
$V = (0.0150)(33.0)$
$V = 0.495~\text{V}$
b) LEDs only allow current flow in one direction due to their semiconductor properties. Reverse current can damage the device.

$V = 0.495~\text{V}$

  1. A battery supplies $24.0~\text{V}$ to a circuit with two identical resistors. If the total current is $0.800~\text{A}$, what is the resistance of each resistor?

Parent formula:
$R_{total} = \frac{V}{I}$
$R_{series} = R_1 + R_2$
$\frac{1}{R_{parallel}} = \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2}$

$V = 24.0~\text{V}$
$I = 0.800~\text{A}$

$R_{total} = \frac{V}{I}$
$R_{total} = 30.0~\Omega$
If series: $R_{each} = 15.0~\Omega$
If parallel: $R_{each} = 60.0~\Omega$

$R_{total} = 30.0~\Omega$
$R_{each,series} = 15.0~\Omega$
$R_{each,parallel} = 60.0~\Omega$

  1. a) Calculate the resistance of a car starter motor ($12.6~\text{V}$, $185~\text{A}$).
    b) How much charge flows through it in $3.00~\text{s}$?

Parent formula:
$R = \frac{V}{I}$
$Q = I \times t$

$V = 12.6~\text{V}$
$I = 185~\text{A}$
$t = 3.00~\text{s}$

a) $R = \frac{V}{I}$
$R = \frac{12.6}{185}$
$R = 0.0681~\Omega$
b) $Q = It$
$Q = (185)(3.00)$
$Q = 555~\text{C}$

$R = 0.0681~\Omega$
$Q = 555~\text{C}$

  1. a) What is the effective resistance of a laptop charging circuit ($19.5~\text{V}$, $3.33~\text{A}$)?
    b) How much charge is transferred in $2.00~\text{hours}$?

Parent formula:
$R = \frac{V}{I}$
$Q = I \times t$

$V = 19.5~\text{V}$
$I = 3.33~\text{A}$
$t = 2.00~\text{hr} = 7200~\text{s}$

a) $R = \frac{V}{I}$
$R = \frac{19.5}{3.33}$
$R = 5.86~\Omega$
b) $Q = It$
$Q = (3.33)(7200)$
$Q = 24000~\text{C}$

$R = 5.86~\Omega$
$Q = 24000~\text{C}$
